title: Today’s Papers – Italy pays tribute to Baresi
description: Italian football is in mourning, and on Saturday its three great sports dailies handed their front pages over entirely to Franco Baresi, the Milan and Italy legend who died on Friday aged 66.According...
fullText:
Italian football is in mourning, and on Saturday its three great sports dailies handed their front pages over entirely to Franco Baresi, the Milan and Italy legend who died on Friday aged 66.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the country has lost “a giant.” Beneath a photograph of Baresi lifting the European Cup, the pink paper leads with “Mio Capitano”, “My Captain”, recalling how the boy nicknamed “il Piscinin” grew into a colossus who won everything and stood by his Milan even through their relegation to Serie B.

Inside, tributes and interviews pour in from those who knew him best, among them former coach Fabio Capello, ex-team-mate Christian Panucci and Rossoneri great Gianni Rivera, alongside columns from the likes of Luigi Garlando and Beppe Bergomi.

Corriere dello Sport: Strikes a similar chord with “6 per sempre”, “Six forever”, a nod to the shirt number Milan retired in his honour. Under the line “Addio capitano,” the paper hails “elegance become legend” and reports that Italian football is “in tears,” having “lost a beat of our heart.”

It traces the arc of a life defined by 21 trophies, from the 1982 World Cup to three European Cups under Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello, and carries the words of long-time defensive partner Alessandro Costacurta, who recalled how Baresi “knew how to lead you through his conduct.”

Turin’s Tuttosport keeps it simple: “Un capitano,” above the dates 1960-2026 and another image of Baresi and the European Cup. Its tributes reach beyond the trophies to the moments that defined the man, the courage of his tearful stand at Pasadena in the 1994 World Cup final, and the 39 red roses he laid in memory of the Heysel victims, “from a champion of humanity.”

The papers also carry the details of a nation’s farewell. Baresi’s funeral will be held on Tuesday 4 August at 11am at the Basilica of Sant’Ambrogio in Milan, with the Rossoneri squad unable to attend as they are away on their pre-season tour. FIGC president Giovanni Malagò has ordered a minute’s silence before every friendly played in Italy this weekend.

title: Stephen A. Smith on Fauci: ‘You can’t show up on Capitol Hill and plead the Fifth 111 times’
description: Sports commentator Stephen A. Smith said Thursday that former White House chief medical adviser Anthony Fauci should have answered lawmakers’ questions during the hostile Senate hearing earlier this w...
fullText:
Sports commentator Stephen A. Smith said Thursday that former White House chief medical adviser Anthony Fauci should have answered lawmakers' questions during the hostile Senate hearing earlier this week instead of invoking his Fifth Amendment rights.

Smith argued that Fauci owed the public an explanation after serving as the face of the nation's COVID-19 response.

"As it strictly pertains to the coronavirus pandemic, my attitude is, with you being the face that you have been, you can't show up on Capitol Hill and plead the Fifth 111 times," he told NewsNation's Chris Cuomo. "You just can't do that. That's not right. You've got to answer some questions."

During a three-hour hearing before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Wednesday, Fauci pleaded the Fifth 111 times as Republicans blasted him over his handling of the pandemic and accused the doctor of covering up the U.S.'s involvement in gain-of-function research that could have caused the spread of the virus.

Smith acknowledged that Fauci, who led the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for nearly 40 years, may have had a legitimate legal reason to remain silent — pointing to a pardon he received from former President Biden on his final day in office for potential offenses between Jan. 1, 2014, and Jan. 19, 2025.

"Anything that he said clearly could potentially incriminate him and could give them fodder to come after him for future potential transgressions, and they can go after him that way, and I certainly don't want an 85-year-old man thrown in jail, particularly with his exemplary service," the commentator told NewsNation.

During the hearing, Republicans argued Fauci had no basis to invoke the Fifth Amendment, when the doctor continuously repeated his one-line phrase: "On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution."

Before the hearing, committee Chair Rand Paul (R-Ky.) released more than 1,000 pages of Fauci's personal diary and work records. Fauci condemned the move as an attempt at "embarrassing and intimidating" him.

Paul, who has sought to indict Fauci, is also threatening to hold him in contempt after the hearing.

While Democrats praised the doctor for his decades of public service and leadership in the infectious disease space, many Republicans accused him of being responsible for COVID-19-related deaths, vaccine injuries and destroying the American public's trust in the healthcare system.

title: Rugby v cricket - England's George swaps sports to help tackle MND
description: England and Saracens' Jamie George on why he and Somerset's Lewis Gregory are playing a charity cricket match to raise money for motor neurone disease charities.
fullText:
Rugby might be England and Saracens hooker Jamie George's first love but cricket is still a regular part of his sporting life and career.

It's why he and his club team-mates did not need much persuading to 

"We [Saracens] do play [cricket] - our warm-up [for] every rugby session - summer, winter, snowing, rain - is one hand, one bounce," George told BBC Radio Somerset.

"The boys love it because they're mad-keen cricket fans."

George will skipper 'Team Rugby' for the game on 19 August at the County Ground in Taunton, in a side that also includes current and former England internationals Owen Farrell, Elliot Daly, Ben Earl and Max Malins.

Somerset captain Lewis Gregory will lead the opposition to tie in with his testimonial year, with Surrey and England's Jamie Overton and former Somerset all-rounder Peter Trego also on the teamsheet.

George was in the stand at the County Ground for a T20 match earlier this season and bumped into Somerset all-rounder Tom Kohler-Cadmore, who was injured at the time, and the idea was touted.

"I'm actually doing a testimonial year next year and I said the dream would be to play a game of cricket somewhere like this," George, who captained England during this summer's Nations Series, said.

"[Kohler-Cadmore] said: 'Why don't we do it for Lewis' testimonial?' I thought it's an unbelievable opportunity."

Back with his Saracens team, George instantly started pulling a side together.

"We were out to dinner and within seconds we were coming up with a batting order," he said.

"I suggested we should merge teams and they said 'no, we want to take them on', categorically rugby versus cricket."

While George and his team-mates are not short of experience, with hundreds of international caps and English Prem games between them, on the cricket pitch it is, of course, a different story compared to their opponents.

However, the rugby squad do have some experience to call upon.

Daly represented Surrey as a teenager and played for England at age-grade level, while Earl similarly played for Kent as an under-15.

"They're both very handy so at least we'll get some runs on the board and then we'll have to scramble around a bit," George, 35, said.

As for what kind of player George will be? "Like a Daren Sammy [former West Indies T20 World Cup-winning captain] type role, I would not bowl and I'd bat at nine or 10 and just be there for morale," he said.

"I'm an old man now but I used to play a lot of cricket back when I was at school."

Gregory, who is Somerset's all-time leading T20 wicket-taker, is happy the game is being played on his turf rather than the other way around and in a rugby match.

"A lot of our lads are excited to see the rugby boys in action and it will be nice to put them under a bit of pressure rather than it being in a rugby game, because that could be a little bit messy," he said.

The decision to support the MND Association was also an easy one for both Gregory and George, with former players in both rugby and cricket having been diagnosed with the disease in recent years.

MND is a neurological condition which affects the brain and spinal cord, and can affect a person's ability to talk, walk and breathe.

Former England and Gloucestershire fast bowler David 'Syd' Lawrence died in 2025, having been diagnosed with MND the year previously.

Doddie Weir, the former Scotland lock, died in 2022, six years after being diagnosed with MND, and having raised millions of pounds and awareness to combat the disease, while former Gloucester lock Ed Slater and former England captain Lewis Moody both live with MND.

"It's a horrible disease and that's why the rugby and the cricket communities are very similar, there's a lot of crossover between the two," George said.

"We look after our own and we want to try to do everything we can to raise as much awareness and hopefully find a cure."

title: Can boxing ‘addiction’ ever be cured? Pain of retiring explored in new Sky documentary
description: IN FOCUS: Alex Pattle dives into the Sky Sports film ‘The Final Round’ and speaks to champion turned pundit Johnny Nelson, a key voice in the documentary
fullText:
Sky Sports’s new documentary is stacked with sobering soundbites. In one scene, boxing coach Joe Gallagher recalls hearing a mother ask her son: “Are all the lows worth that one high?” The answer, of course, was “yes”. As Gallagher puts it: “Everyone wants their own Rocky story.”

But as Sky explores, that doesn’t always mean a rousing underdog story. Rocky’s sequels showed Sylvester Stallone’s character struggling with retirement, and this is the premise of The Final Round.

Releasing on Friday, the film features interviews with former world champions like Johnny Nelson and Josh Warrington, while Gallagher and Dominic Ingle are among the coaches to speak, promoter Eddie Hearn features, and commentator Andy Clarke weaves together themes of “addiction”, sacrifice, and ego.

The documentary even includes one of the final interviews with the late, great Ricky Hatton, whose internal fights after retiring matched any that he had in the ring.

Many boxers tell themselves, “‘I’ve got one more good fight in me,’” Hatton says. “Nine times out of 10, you haven’t. That was the case with me.”

Indeed, in 2022, a 42-year-old Hatton boxed Marco Antonio Barrera in an exhibition, and he was even due for another before his untimely death last September.

“Ego never leaves a fighter, and that’s the problem,” Nelson says. It outlasts the “fire”, he adds, shrewdly touching on an unfair fight between the two emotions.

Yet it’s not just about fire and ego; a question of identity arises, as does a fear of life post-boxing. Retirement is “frightening”, says heavyweight veteran Dave Allen, who reversed his own exit from the sport. “Apart from ‘Dad’, I’m just a boxer. I’m not even David, the normal human being.”

Warrington, whose boxing future is up in the air at the time of writing, explains: “I wake up on fight day and it’s like everything’s brighter, everything smells better, I’m more alert... that’s an unreal feeling.” And then the kicker: “Once that stops, you’ll never feel it again.”

Does this explain Tyson Fury’s five false retirements? Perhaps. They get their own spotlight in the documentary, as do comebacks that occur decades after retirement: for example, a 58-year-old Mike Tyson facing a 27-year-old YouTuber, Jake Paul, in 2024.

The film touches on how boxers don’t just miss the buzz of fight night, but also the camaraderie of their gyms, while the financial turmoil that has afflicted many fighters gets significant screen time.

Most boxers need a second job, and promoter and manager Steve Wood explains: “Ninety per cent of the fighters I look after are not earning enough to pay tax. I’ve had a couple of world champions; they’re the only two likely to be able to retire comfortably.”

In an interview with The Independent, Nelson touches on all of these topics, as well as his plans to create a proper pension scheme for boxers – something his own promoter, Eddie’s father Barry Hearn, attempted unsuccessfully.

Barry tried putting a small percentage of boxers’ purses towards a pension, but fighters’ distrust and/or short-term thinking thwarted the plan. Nelson, who toyed with his own comeback nine years after retiring, reflects on receiving a £97,000 pension from Hearn several years ago, inspiring the 59-year-old.

Nelson wants to create a scheme that would pay £2,000 into a pension for each boxer every year, as long as the fighter competes two to three times annually and puts 5 per cent of their purse into the same pension – with the money coming from a combination of TV companies, government grants, and private sponsorship. Nelson has spoken to the British Boxing Board of Control, figures in parliament, Scottish Widows, and potential financiers while trying to get the scheme off the ground.

“If I was a parent and my son wanted to box, I wouldn’t want him to box for a career, because they’ve got nothing to show for it,” Nelson says. “There’s no aftercare. Everybody’s running for the trees, nobody wants to take responsibility for the fighters creating the entertainment.

“The amount of household names I could tell you that are absolutely on their ass, they’ve got nothing, and that financial pressure on top of the other effects of boxing has accumulated over the years. How can your mental health be stable? How can it be?”

In general, Nelson articulates the existence of a boxer with ease.

“That animalistic instinct we have, there’s nothing you can adapt it to in everyday life – not an office or anything like that, because it’s barbaric,” he says. “It’s a very lonely existence. Your wife, brother, mother, sister don’t get it. The aches and pains are lonely, the thought processes are lonely.

“You do it first for the love of it, then money comes into it, then ups and downs, so we still do it – but resentfully. You’ve not got time to have a full-time job, so [you may think]: ‘People see me on a dizzy high, and then I’ve got to go and work on a building site. God, I've got to deal with the shame of that.’

“You’re resentful of how human nature can change: when you retire, people no longer look up to you as an amazing fighter. ‘He’s overweight, he’s not who he was.’ They talk to you like they talk to anybody, whereas when you’re a fighter, they talk to you with respect.”

Nelson is now one of the most thoughtful and respected pundits in boxing, but he could not have foreseen this future while immersed in his past.

“I thought boxing was the only option I had,” he reflects. “I left school with the reading and writing ability of a 10-year-old. I wasn’t thick – I just wasn’t academically astute – but I thought I was. I’d got nothing on paper to say, ‘Johnny is really good with people,’ so that wisdom doesn’t get you a job. What gets you a job is a diploma, work experience. So, panic set in. I could have easily ended up in prison.”

As The Final Round shows, boxing can be its own kind of prison, but a champion who escaped relatively early and safely was Anthony Crolla, who retired on a win just before turning 33.

“You can’t let boxing take more from you than you take from boxing,” he says astutely in the film. If only it were that simple.

title: PFL, Jake Paul’s MVP merge to form new global combat sports company
description: Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.
fullText:
Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.

 The new company will operate under the MVP banner, led by Co-Founders and Board Members Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian. Meanwhile, former PFL CEO John Martin will serve as CEO and Board Member of the new league. MVP’s boxing business and blockbuster live events will continue under Bidarian. Existing PFL shareholders 885 Capital and affiliated entities Knighthead Capital Management will be the founding investors of the new league, committing new capital.

 The new league vows to work under a “fighter-first” philosophy, seemingly challenging rival Ultimate Fighting Championship. While the UFC has been severely criticized over minimum profit share for athletes, the new combat sports league promises equitable compensation. The new league also plans to encourage athletes to build their brands inside and outside of competition, probably hinting at freedom to choose sponsors.

“We started MVP to disrupt a broken model,” Jake Paul, co-founder of Most Valuable Promotions, said in a press release. “We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernized stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade. We now have a scaled platform to give today's fans what they want: elite talent mixed with culture, lifestyle, and massive social velocity. MVP was always bigger than me and bigger than any one fighter. MVP is an inevitable movement that needs to happen for the athletes, and now we have all the resources we need to build something that changes this sport forever. title: NBC Sports Philadelphia weighing adding courtside voice for Sixers after LeBron James arrival
description: NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer. “I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre-…
fullText:
NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer.

“I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre- and postgame interviews, analysis, all of that,” Matcham said. “It’s a very hard job to do.”

For years, NBC Sports Philadelphia and its predecessor, Comcast SportsNet, used reporters like Serena Winters and Taryn Hatcher to fill that kind of role for the Sixers. That stopped in 2020, when the network began eliminating in-arena and in-game reporting jobs across its properties as basketball and hockey seasons wrapped that year, according to Crossing Broad’s Kevin Kinkead. Hatcher stayed on covering the Phillies for five more seasons after that before her contract lapsed at the end of 2025 and NBC Sports Philadelphia cut the position rather than renew it. Kinkead later reported that the network and Hatcher had discussed a freelance arrangement that would have let her take on other work at the same time, but the talks ended without an agreement over what Kinkead’s sources described as a standard contract disagreement, not any real conflict between the two sides.

That left NBC Sports Philadelphia without anyone in that role for the Sixers’ 2025-26 season, and the roster now taking shape gives the network far less room to go another year without one.

“If you get a generational talent on your team, it could easily become a situation where the people that work for us are burnt out by December, and you don’t want that,” Matcham said. “You need extra help.”

The shape of the new role hasn’t been decided, and Matcham said she’s been deliberate about not defaulting to the title NBC Sports Philadelphia has used for that kind of position in the past. The network cut its last remaining in-arena reporting jobs across its properties, including the Sixers, starting in 2020, and whatever gets added back now won’t simply be a return to that old model.

“As I’m talking to my colleagues, I’m not even calling it a reporter role because I feel like it’s going to give them a stereotype I don’t necessarily mean,” Matcham said.

Among the options Matcham described is bypassing a generalist Sixers reporter altogether in favor of someone hired specifically for James’s orbit, someone with an existing relationship built from prior coverage of him rather than of the team broadly.

The Scott-Abdelnaby broadcast finished 29th out of 30 teams in AA’s 2025-26 local NBA announcer rankings, the third straight season in that spot. The most common grade fans gave them was a C, and roughly six in ten voters gave them a passing grade at all. Several comments also cited the absence of Hatcher as a drag on the broadcast.

Hatcher spent eight years at NBC Sports Philadelphia covering all four major Philadelphia teams, most recently working Phillies home games alongside Tom McCarthy and John Kruk, but since her departure has been selective about new roles while managing a health situation. Matcham defended the decision at the time, telling the Philadelphia Business Journal the network wanted “to add to our storytelling in new ways” and that the position was being eliminated.

Whatever title the network settles on, it will be trying to recreate, under different terms, the exact kind of presence it decided a year ago it could do without.

title: 'Time for change is now' - MVP and PFL merge
description: Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League merge to create "a combat sports company for the new era".
fullText:
Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League have merged to create "a combat sports company for the new era".

The newly formed partnership will be led by MVP co-founders Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian, with PFL head John Martin also on the board and continuing to operate as CEO.

The PFL will move under the brand of MVP to bring together a roster of more than 300 fighters across boxing and mixed martial arts (MMA).

MVP focused on boxing when launching in 2021 but ventured into MMA for the first time in May.

"We started MVP to disrupt a broken model," Paul said.

"We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernised stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade.

"To all current MVP and PFL fighters, things just got bigger. To fighters fighting in other organisations, we are open for business when you are contractually free. The time for change is now."

MVP's first - and only - MMA show set a new record for the most-watched MMA event in the United States, with a "minute audience" of 12.4 million viewers as Ronda Rousey beat Gina Carrano, according to broadcaster Netflix.

Rousey's 15-second win peaked at 17 million viewers globally on Netflix, shattering the previous record of nine million.

The PFL has attempted to innovate the MMA space since launching in 2017, opting for a league-based system with points gained in each fight before season-ending play-offs.

It initially offered prize money of $1m (£750,000) but made sweeping changes in 2025 and reduced that to $500,000 (£374,000).

"Over the past seven years, PFL has built the world's number two global MMA company," Martin said.

"We're not just combining companies, we're bringing an entire combat sports community together and creating a more powerful platform to accelerate growth.

"One company, one global stage, millions of fans - and we're only just getting started."

It comes after MVP announced a new partnership with Matchroom Boxing on Tuesday, with the aim of creating more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

MVP has invested heavily in women's boxing over the past five years and boasts an impressive stable of world champions, including Britons Caroline Dubois and Chantelle Cameron.

title: Cricket & archery well placed for Commonwealths spot
description: Cricket, archery and shooting are among the sports well placed to regain their spot at the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030.
fullText:
Cricket, archery and shooting are among the sports well placed to regain their spot at the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030.

Only 10 sports were included in the ongoing Glasgow Games because of the rushed build-up after the Australian state of Victoria pulled out as hosts.

Discussions on the sporting programme remain ongoing between Commonwealth Sport, sporting federations and the Indian organising committee for the next Games, which will be held in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

Speaking to BBC Sport, Commonwealth Sport chief executive Katie Sadlier would not be drawn on the process but India Olympic Association's Raghu Iyer said: "There are many sports who will feel they have missed out.

"There are sports in which India has done very well, shooting, archery and many other sports."

Pushed on whether that puts cricket, which was included for Birmingham 2022 for the first time in 24 years as a women's-only T20 event, archery and shooting at the top of the queue, Iyer added: "While I do not have the mandate to talk about any of these, you have been pretty interesting with the choices you have mentioned…"

"We also want to have sports that India have traditionally done well in," he said.

Boxer Abdul - grandson of dictator - disqualified for headbutt

Cricket's cause is helped by the fact at least two team sports will be added for 2030. Hockey and rugby sevens would be other options.

Badminton, 3x3 basketball and 3x3 wheelchair basketball, beach volleyball, cycling, diving, judo, rhythmic gymnastics, squash, triathlon and para triathlon and wrestling are other sports under consideration.

India can also propose two new sports as host nation and push others that have significance at home. No final decisions have been made.

Ahmedabad will be the Commonwealth's centenary Games and events will held in the 120,000-seater Narendra Modi Stadium, which has hosted two cricket World Cup finals in recent years.

India has also expressed a keen interest in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, with this potentially a key step in the road.

"Any sporting event will be a step towards that," Iyer said. "We are looking purely at ensuring that these Commonwealth Games are one of the best that have been held."

The reduced programme in Glasgow has helped slash the cost of hosting the Games from around £800m to £160m.

Organisers have been keen to claim this repurposed structure will be cheaper and more appealing for future hosts, but the sporting programme will rise to 17 in Ahmedabad.

"17 is, we think, the right number," Sadlier said.

"The Victoria Games was 26 sports. We recognised we needed to reset and bring the Games into something that was affordable around the Commonwealth.

"What we have done here has been brilliant but we will bring back a few sports. We won't go beyond that number."

Sadlier also rejected concerns around the cut through of the Glasgow Games, given there has been no live television coverage on a major channel in the UK.

"We have got more broadcast deals signed for this Games than we ever have," she said.

"Globally, the reach has been exceptional. On socials we broke the targets from Birmingham last week. It has been an amazingly covered Games."

fullText:

title: Brazil bans defender Gabriel until Pec returns from broken leg injury
description: Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg, Brazil's sports court said.
fullText:
July 29 (UPI) -- Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg injury, Brazil's sports court said.

Brazil's Superior Court of Sports Justice, or STJD, announced the ruling Tuesday. Pec fractured a tibia after Gabriel tackled him during a 2-1 win over Internacional on July 22 in Porto Alegre, Brazil.

Gabriel, who attended the STJD committee hearing for the ruling, apologized to Pec.

"I had the feeling that I would get to the ball first, and I did," Gabriel said. "Since the field was quite slippery and wet, I ended up hitting the ball and then I didn't have time to pull my leg back, and that's how this somewhat harder tackle happened, but without any intention of causing harm to my fellow professional or any malice."

The defender was given a red card for the incident. Pec's injury required surgery. Gabriel's ban, which will end when Pec returns to training, is capped at 180 days.

"I've always been a loyal guy and I've always gone onto the field to, above all, defend my club and my dream," Gabriel said. "I've always tried to be as loyal as possible to my teammates and opponents. It was a completely unfortunate incident.

"I apologized to him and offered my help. I asked him to forgive me for not having had any ill intent, and all I could do at that moment was pray for him.

"Since that night, it's been incredibly difficult for me. My whole life I've prepared for moments of happiness, and instead, it's been sleepless nights."

Internacional (5-9-6) sits at No. 16 in the Brazilian Serie A standings. Cruzeiro (7-7-6) sits at No. 11, 17 points behind first-place Palmeiras (13-2-5).

title: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
description: Falcons take 6-foot-3 Texas WR in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
fullText:
There are some major question marks surrounding the Atlanta Falcons' roster as the team prepares to kick off training camp this week in Flowery Branch. From the starting quarterback competition to the battle for the No. 2 wide receiver job, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has much to figure out over the next month.

The team signed former first-round pick Jahan Dotson to replace speedster Darnell Mooney, but it's fair to question whether or not he's capable of filling that role. Dotson's career stats suggest otherwise, however, it's tough to produce when you're stuck behind two elite receivers, as he was in Philadelphia.

Former Georgia wide receiver Zachariah Branch appears to have a bright future, assuming his effectiveness isn't hindered by his lack of size. Depending on how this season goes, the Falcons may or may not be looking for a new No. 2 wide receiver in 2027.

Atlanta lands a perfect complement to Drake London in a new CBS Sports mock draft from Mike Renner. The Falcons were projected to take Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman with the sixth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

"Cam Coleman is a wildly explosive 6-foot-3, 200-pound wideout who spent the past two seasons stuck with poor quarterback play at Auburn," wrote Renner. "That changes this year as he heads to Texas to pair with Arch Manning. He should be a household name by season's end."

Coleman racked up 93 receptions for 1,306 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns (14.0 yards per catch) over the last two seasons at Auburn. The Falcons have dealt with similar quarterback issues over the past few years, so Coleman would feel right at home in Atlanta.

The Falcons did re-sign London to a four-year, $141 million contract extension during the offseason, however, there is still a clear lack of depth behind him. Branch could be a long-term option in the slot with No. 2 upside, but it wouldn't hurt to add to the receiver room in 2027.

For now, Atlanta is set to kick off training camp with its current wide receiver group. Although, we wouldn't be surprised to see the team add someone like Stefon Diggs or Keenan Allen before camp ends.

title: Italy’s Sports minister slams Azzurri’s Andrea Pirlo mess-up

fullText:
Italian football finds itself in the middle of a crisis again, as Andrea Pirlo’s candidacy for the Azzurri role has gone up in smoke. There have been increasing doubts about the future of Paolo Maldini too and now, Italy’s sports minister Andrea Abodi has made his views clear about the matter.

Now, Pirlo will definitely not be the next manager of the national team. This is largely due to his links with a FonBet, a Russian betting company and this didn’t sit well with many at FIGC, even if it went against the technical director Maldini’s wishes.

Now, Abodi has been asked about the matter and he has made it clear that things like these shouldn’t be happening in Calcio.

He told Piacenza Hub Network – via Di Marzio: Pirlo’s resignation from the Azzurri bench? It’s news that speaks for itself. It’s a situation we would have liked to have changed with greater speed and with a shared purpose that hasn’t materialised. Now we have to make up for a poor showing.”

The outcome of the Pirlo saga is arguably something that can only unfold in Italian football, embarrassingly enough. It is a classic case of putting politics over sport, while hiring a sporting figure who should be backed to the helm. title: USA250: The 10 greatest college athletes from Nebraska
description: As part of USA TODAY Sports' USA 250 initiative, here's a look at the top 10 greatest college athletes to ever play in the state of Nebraska:
fullText:
Nebraska is a fascinating state to delve into in regard to college sports history, as it has a burgeoning sports scene without the imposing influence of professional sports.

The University of Nebraska's Memorial Stadium has sold out since the 1960s. The College World Series takes place in Omaha. Nebraska women's volleyball holds the world record for attendance at a women's sporting event.

And it isn't just a matter of circumstance. The programs built the loyalty. The Tom Osborne Nebraska-Oklahoma-Barry Switzer football rivalry is the stuff of legend, the 1990s Cornhuskers are still spoken of in reverential tones. Creighton basketball went from Missouri Valley powerhouse to Big East staple. And Nebraska women's volleyball has one of the most passionate followings among college sports as a whole.

From all of that loyalty is borne legendary figures. Across the state and across sports, Nebraska has the athletes to run with nearly any state in the country. Paring that list down to 10 proved to be an extremely difficult task. But here are the 10 Nebraska college athletes who managed to set themselves apart.

Nebraska of the 1990s was dominant. And Tommie Frazier was one of the team's great players in the decade. After he got his feet wet as a freshman, Frazier came into his own as a sophomore. Though he rarely threw the ball in Tom Osborne's ruthless triple option offense, but he passed for 3,521 yards in his career and added 1,955 yards and 36 touchdowns on the ground. But Frazier's legacy defies stats: Nebraska won 36 of 37 games in his final three seasons. The lone loss came to Florida State at the end of the 1993 season in the Orange Bowl that was a matchup of two unbeatens. Frazier would then lead the Cornhuskers to back-to-back titles the next two season and finish runner-up to Eddie George in the voting for the 1995 Heisman Trophy.

USA 250 LISTS: Alaska | Alabama | Arizona | Arkansas | California | Colorado | Connecticut | Delaware | Florida | Georgia | Hawaii | Idaho | Illinois | Indiana | Iowa | Kansas | Kentucky | Louisiana | Maine | Maryland | Massachusetts | Michigan | Minnesota | Mississippi | Missouri | Montana | Nebraska | Nevada | New Hampshire | New Jersey

Born in Omaha in 1935, Bob Gibson is one of the most dynamic pitchers in baseball history. His stuff is the stuff of legends, and he got his start with the Creighton Bluejays. A two-sport athlete, Gibson played baseball and basketball for his hometown university. He finished his career on the hardwood as the school's third-leading scorer at the time with 1,272 points. Unfortunately, his baseball stats are lost in the annals of history, it's known he was an outfielder and a pitcher for Creighton. Gibson had a legendary pitching career with the St. Louis Cardinals, and was named to Creighton's Hall of Fame in 1968.

When you think about hard-nosed Huskers, you think about Mike Rozier. After setting the single-season school record with 1,689 rushing yards as a junior in 1982, he shattered his own mark the following season as part of one of the greatest offenses in college history. Rozier put up an absurd 2,148 yards and an NCAA-record 29 touchdowns on the ground on his way to winning the 1983 Heisman Trophy. That Nebraska offense averaged over 50 points per game with Rozier serving as the focal point, and though it came up short of a national title with an Orange Bowl loss to Miami, it's remembered as one of the great seasons in Nebraska football.

PROGRAM RANKINGS: Top 25 | Big Ten | SEC | ACC | Big 12

Ask someone born in the '90s the most dominant defensive player they watched in college growing up, and dollars to donuts Ndamukong Suh's name is going to come up. One of the most overpowering linemen in history, Suh turned otherwise-stalwart offensive linemen into sleds. Suh's 2009 season is the stuff of college football legend: He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting, the best at the time for a solely defensive player since Steve Emtman in 1991 after logging 85 tackles with 20½ tackles for a loss and 12 sacks. Suh missing out on the Heisman was widely regarded as a death knell for the hopes of a solely defensive player winning the trophy, and he remains a Nebraska legend to this day.

Johnny Rodgers isn't just etched into the fabric of Nebraska. He's woven into the tapestry of college football. A receiver, running back, and return specialist, record after record fell before Rodgers' speed. A Walter Camp Player of the Year and Heisman Trophy winner in 1971, Rodgers finished his career with the two highest all-purpose yards seasons in Nebraska history, along with the record for most career all-purpose yards. He still holds the record for career receiving touchdowns and ended his time on the gridiron with the most points accounted for in Nebraska history. Often considered among the best return men in college football history, Rodgers was precursor for the athlete position in college sports.

Eric Crouch evokes one of the last gasps of an era of greatness for Nebraska football. Crouch led the Big 12 in rushing touchdowns in each of his final three seasons and posted a 35-7 record as a starter. He had a dominant senior campaign in 2001 to win the Heisman Trophy, edging out Florida quarterback Rex Grossman. For the season, Crouch rushed for 1,115 yards and 18 touchdowns and threw for 1,510 yards, while leading the Cornhuskers to the Bowl Championship Series title game in the Rose Bowl. Though Nebraska would lose to Miami (Fla.) in his final game, Crouch's legacy has endured as one of the most dynamic athletes in Cornhusker football history.

While Nebraska football is a dynasty, Nebraska volleyball is an institution all of its own. The Cornhuskers are five-time national champions and have four championships since the turn of the century. Pavan is one of the most decorated volleyball players in Nebraska history. She was a four-time first-team All-American and set multiple records with the Cornhuskers while making Lincoln a destination for volleyball. Pavan helped Nebraska to a national championship in 2006 and four consecutive Big 12 titles. She is quintessentially Nebraska volleyball, and volleyball is quintessentially Nebraska.

Why wouldn't Nebraska get two volleyball players on this list? Joining Pavan is Jordan Larson, who was also part of the 2006 championship team. Larson was a three-time All-American and had over 1,000 kills and digs in her Nebraska career. Her best season was in 2008, when she earned multiple accolades before becoming an Olympic star as well, culminating in a gold medal win in Tokyo in the 2020 Summer Games.

Fresh off her college career when she was a four-time first-team All-American, Frahm is already a Nebraska softball legend. Born in Papillion, Frahm started her career at Oklahoma, winning two national championships with a 44-2 record as the star pitcher for Sooners. Frahm transferred to Nebraska after her sophomore season, but was injured in her first game in 2024. She returned the following year to help Nebraska to the super regionals for the first time since 2014. Frahm was national player of the year as a senior, leading the Cornhuskers to their first Women's College World Series appearance since 2013,. A true two-way superstar, she posted a 47-14 record pitching over two seasons at Nebraska with an ERA of 1.44. She slugged 1.418 as a Cornhusker with 43 home runs.

title: Fanatics Fest NYC: Inter's booth in the heart of New York

fullText:
For the second consecutive year, Inter took centre stage at Fanatics Fest NYC, the biggest sports culture event in the United States, bringing to New York an experience that showcased the Club far beyond the football pitch.

The Nerazzurri booth welcomed thousands of visitors, offering a vibrant space where football, design, music and entertainment came together, once again highlighting the strength of the Inter brand on the international stage.

Inspired by contemporary industrial aesthetics and the concept of scaffolding, the booth drew on the shared urban language of Milano and New York. This design approach gave shape to the "Different Fields. Same Belonging." concept, the message behind the launch of the new Away Kit, portraying Inter as a Club capable of forging authentic connections across different worlds. Designed to express the Nerazzurri identity through a multifaceted visual language, the installation stood at the crossroads of sport, creativity and urban culture.

The booth took visitors on a journey through the Nerazzurri's past, present and future. The new kits, lifestyle collections, community-focused content, Inter's connection with the world of music and the Club's heritage brought the space to life, enhanced by a network of indoor and outdoor screens designed to make the experience even more immersive.

One of the booth's standout attractions was the display of the trophies from the Club's historic Double, attracting thousands of fans eager to admire up close two lasting reminders of an unforgettable season.

The fan activation also proved hugely popular. By answering a series of five questions, visitors were able to create their own Inter Emblem – a personalised symbol inspired by their identity and the way they experience their Nerazzurri passion. Each design was transformed into an exclusive pin, printed in real time and presented to fans at the end of the experience. The activation placed the community at its heart while also giving participants the chance to win a trip to Milano to discover some of the Club's most iconic locations, from San Siro to Inter HQ.

Over the course of the four-day event, the booth became one of Fanatics Fest's main attractions, welcoming Inter Vice President Javier Zanetti and Club Legend Christian Vieri, as well as participants in the Away Kit launch panel, including Dom Innarella, Chxrry, the Evening Elephants and many other Inter Friends.

The Nerazzurri booth proved to be a space that showcased every facet of Inter: a Club with a global voice, building connections between sport, culture and innovation through a shared sense of belonging.

title: Where does Vikings' Caleb Banks land in 2026 NFL Draft redo?
description: Caleb Banks fell from No. 18 to No. 29 in a Sports Illustrated 2026 NFL Draft redo, but the Vikings rookie still remained a first-round talent.
fullText:
Caleb Banks has not played a regular-season snap for the Minnesota Vikings, but his draft value is already being revisited.

In a Sports Illustrated 2026 NFL Draft redo published before training camp, Justin Melo had Banks falling to the Kansas City Chiefs at No. 29 overall. The Vikings originally selected the Florida defensive tackle at No. 18, betting on his rare size, power and upside despite an injury history that complicated his pre-draft evaluation.

Melo sent Banks to Kansas City in place of Peter Woods, writing that the Chiefs prioritized defensive tackle in the original draft but could have landed a better prospect in Banks. He described Banks as a “high-risk, high-reward prospect” and noted that playing next to Chris Jones would have been an ideal environment for the rookie to develop.

For Minnesota, the redo reflects the same tension that surrounded Banks throughout the draft process.

His talent was never difficult to identify. At 6-foot-6 and 327 pounds, Banks has the frame and physical tools teams covet in an interior defender. When healthy and consistent, he has the ability to disrupt blocking schemes, collapse pockets and give the Vikings another young building block for Brian Flores’ defense.

The concern has been availability. Banks twice broke his left foot in the past year, an injury that cost him most of the 2025 season at Florida and required surgery after the NFL scouting combine in March. He later sent a letter to NFL teams identifying the injury as a broken fourth metatarsal and projecting that he would resume football activities in June.

That context explains why a redraft can view Banks two ways. The Vikings may have taken on more risk than some teams preferred at No. 18, but SI’s redo still kept him in the first round. That matters.

Minnesota drafted Banks for what he can become, not just what he was able to show during an injury-shortened final college season. Training camp will provide the first real indication of whether that upside is ready to surface quickly.

title: Should UNC leave the ACC if offered?
description: There are no sports right now, so let’s revisit social media’s most toxic topic.
fullText:
Congress is in the process of trying to solve the problems that the NCAA refuses to fix — leveling the NIL/transfer portal playing field, and figuring how to navigate realignment. Focusing on realignment specifically, one of the options on the table is capping the Big Ten and SEC to a certain amount of schools per conference, and there’s also been a lot of talk about the SEC leaving the NCAA as a whole.

Because, you know, the SEC is too good than to stay in the asylum anymore (sarcasm).

When it comes to the ACC, nobody really knows what the future will hold, but there’s been whispers for years that UNC is a potential target for one of the bigger two conferences and that the school is interested. Here’s the thing: it’s probably been discussed, but the Grant of Rights has become such an issue for any school even thinking about leaving that it’s probably not even worth the conversation, especially now that programs are bleeding money due to revenue sharing with their players. Is that to say UNC couldn’t figure it out? Not necessarily, but it would be a very hard thing to pull off, and I have a feeling they would have to get donors onboard as well.

That said, let’s have some fun and discuss a hypothetical anyway. Let’s say money isn’t an issue to Carolina, they are more than willing to buy their way out of the Grant of Rights, and they begin seriously considering next steps. Would you want them to head to the Big Ten or SEC? Or would you want them to stay in the ACC? There’s good arguments for both sides of this conversation, but ultimately what it comes down to is money vs. tradition. UNC would undoubtedly pull in more money in another conference, but would it be worth losing some of their soul?

title: Sky Sports: Arsenal Chase Two England Stars After Key Injury
description: Arsenal Transfer News: John Stones and Ezri Konsa Interest Makes Sense After William Saliba Injury BlowArsenal have a problem, and it is a serious one. William Saliba, arguably the club’s most impor...
fullText:
Arsenal have a problem, and it is a serious one. William Saliba, arguably the club’s most important defender, is set for a long spell out after suffering a back injury during France’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain. According to Sky Sports, Arsenal are now looking hard at the centre-back market, with John Stones and Ezri Konsa among the names under consideration.

That much is logical. Saliba has “avoided the need for surgery” but still faces “a lengthy period of rehabilitation”. You do not lose a defender of that calibre and pretend your existing depth solves everything. Arsenal have numbers at the back, yes, but top-level sides do not build plans around wishful thinking. They build around certainty, availability and profile.

That is where this story gets interesting. Stones and Konsa are both credible options, both known quantities in the Premier League, and both capable of playing at right-back. The similarity ends there.

Arsenal have already moved to “consolidated their defensive options” by signing Piero Hincapie permanently after his loan from Bayer Leverkusen. They also have Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber and Ben White available, or close to available, across the defensive line.

But context matters. White is only just back in training after the knee injury he suffered in May. Timber has said he is “hopefully back soon” as he recovers from a groin problem. In other words, there are still too many variables. Arteta cannot go into the season knowing Saliba is out for an “extended period” and simply hope the rest of the puzzle pieces stay in place.

That is why the search is centred on players who can handle major minutes quickly, understand positional discipline, and slot into a side that asks defenders to play high, defend space and circulate possession cleanly.

Start with Stones. He is a free agent, which immediately changes the discussion. There is no transfer fee, no drawn-out negotiation with Manchester City, and no need to justify a huge outlay on a player in his thirties. If Arsenal want experienced short-term cover, he is sitting there.

There is also the Arteta factor. He knows the player well from his time at City and has never hidden his admiration. “John is a player I really like,” Arteta said previously. “We followed him before we signed him when I was at City. I worked with him for many years. I know him well and when I look at centre-backs, he has many attributes that I like.”

That quote matters because it tells you this is not casual admiration. Arteta understands exactly what Stones offers, composure on the ball, tactical intelligence, comfort stepping into midfield, and the kind of senior presence that can settle a back line. On a free, that has obvious appeal.

But there is no point dressing up the downside. Stones is 32 and his recent injury record is poor. He managed only 439 Premier League minutes last season, with thigh, calf and muscular issues disrupting him, and only 547 minutes the season before. Those are not minor caveats, they are central facts. Arsenal need cover for an injured defender. Signing another defender with recurring fitness concerns may be cheap, but cheap and sensible are not always the same thing.

Still, if the club’s thinking is to buy time, add experience and avoid spending heavily in a difficult market, Stones is a perfectly rational option.

Konsa is the cleaner football fit. He is younger at 28, more durable, and far more likely to handle the weekly physical demands of a Premier League title race. As reported by Sky Sports, Arsenal have been “exploring the cost of a potential deal for Konsa” but “there is a significant gap in valuation with Villa”. That is the issue in one sentence.

Villa are said to value him at £60m. For a player turning 29 in October, that is a serious fee. It may even be a prohibitive one, depending on the rest of Arsenal’s summer plans.

From a tactical standpoint, however, the attraction is obvious. Konsa plays primarily as a right-sided centre-back, the same side Saliba occupies, and he can cover right-back too. He is reliable in possession, calm under pressure and physically strong. More importantly, he stays fit. He has made at least 33 Premier League starts in five straight seasons, which in itself tells you plenty.

The underlying numbers strengthen the case. According to Opta, Konsa posted the highest ground-duel success rate of any outfield player in the Premier League last season at 73 per cent. That is elite output. Arsenal do not only need a body, they need someone who can defend space aggressively and win his individual battles. Konsa does that.

So yes, he is more expensive than Stones. He should be. He is also a better medium-term answer.

One interesting detail in the reporting is that neither Stones nor Konsa ranks among the 10 most stylistically similar players to Saliba using Twenty3’s similarity tool, although Konsa comes close in 12th. That should not be overstated, but it is worth noting. Replacing Saliba directly is difficult because there are not many defenders with his blend of recovery pace, passing range, composure and authority.

Arsenal are therefore making a compromise, whichever route they take. Stones offers intelligence, pedigree and a free deal, but obvious durability concerns. Konsa offers availability, athleticism and Premier League-tested defending, but at a price Aston Villa have little reason to lower.

There is no magic solution here. If Arsenal want the low-cost, short-term answer, Stones makes sense. If they want the stronger all-round fit for the next two or three seasons, Konsa is the better target. The catch is that one costs wages and risk, the other costs around £60m.

That is the market. You either pay with money or pay with uncertainty. Arsenal now need to choose which bill they are more comfortable settling.

From an Arsenal supporter’s point of view, this feels pretty simple. Saliba being out for a while is bad news, proper bad news, because he is the one defender you do not really replace. You just try to cope without him and make the drop-off as small as possible.

Stones is one of those deals where you instantly see why it might happen. Free transfer, huge experience, knows Arteta, can play football properly. Fine. No issue with that, as long as everyone is honest about the risk. If he misses chunks of the season, nobody can act surprised. The evidence is already there.

Konsa feels safer. Less glamorous, maybe, but probably more useful over the course of a full season. He plays, he defends, he knows the league, and he looks like someone who would slot in without drama. If Villa really want £60m, though, you can understand Arsenal hesitating, especially if there are other positions to sort out.

Personally, the ideal outcome might be the practical one. If the club believe Saliba will be back in a reasonable timeframe, Stones on a smart deal could do the job. If the absence is likely to drag and Arsenal want real security, then they should push harder for Konsa. Either way, doing nothing would be the worst move of the lot.

title: Megan Rapinoe says efforts to bar trans athletes from women's sports are 'attack on women in society'
description: Megan Rapinoe appeared on "The View" to argue that transgender athlete bans are a broader attack on women's empowerment and confidence overall.
fullText:
Former U.S. Women's National Team star Megan Rapinoe said Tuesday that efforts to bar transgender athletes from competing in women's sports amount to "an attack on women in society," arguing the debate extends far beyond questions of fairness in athletic competition.

Appearing on ABC's "The View," Rapinoe dismissed arguments that restrictions on transgender athletes are primarily about protecting girls' and women's sports. Instead, she argued, opponents are using the issue as part of a broader campaign against women's empowerment.

"They're going after trans people in sports, and they're using this as a wedge issue because we love sports. And, you know, we don't want our little girls to be unsafe in sports. And it's like, 'Unsafe from who? But okay,'" Rapinoe said.

California Billionaire Tom Steyer Defends Trans Athletes In High School Sports As Governor's Race Heats Up

"But now we're using this as like, an overarching thing, when really what we're attacking women, we're saying, 'If you look like this as a woman, you can play, if you look like this as a woman.' There's a bill in Washington happening right now that's going to require all girls, just like full stop, to go through a sex test, an invasive, like examining their genitals to see if they're a woman," Rapinoe said.

Initiative IL26-638, according to the House Republican Caucus, would "prohibit students it defines as 'biologically male' from competing in certain school athletic activities intended for female students only. It would require verification of biological sex by students' healthcare providers."

Trans Athletes Drop Lawsuit To Gain Access To Girls' Sports In New Hampshire After Scotus Ruling

"They don't like women in sports because it helps us with confidence and power," Rapinoe said. "And we see so many women in the C-suite played elite level sports. It's just great for you physically and all of it. But it's an attack on women in society."

Wnba Player Faces Backlash Over Op-ed Criticizing Ioc For Policy To Protect Women's Sports

In a recent article in Marie Claire entitled, "Anti-Trans Legislation Isn't About 'Protecting Girls'—It's About Distracting Us From What Matters," Rapinoe wrote,

"The truth is, trans people have been competing in sports for decades, and will continue to participate as this smoke screen from bad faith legislators and anti-LGBT groups cloak the real damage being done. As with so many other manufactured issues we fall for, women and girls will suffer the most."

Rapinoe did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: The 'Tarps Off' Trend Explained
description: Over the last two months, huge swaths of baseball stadiums have been taken over by fans spinning their shirts over their heads, but this phenomenon goes back further than you might think. Here's how the "Tarps Off" trend started and swept the sports world.
fullText:
One of the biggest fan traditions to emerge from the 2026 baseball season didn't start with a mascot or a chant. Instead, it involved fans ripping off their shirts and spinning them over their heads in an attempt to fire up the stadium during big moments.

Known as the "Tarps Off Trend," the celebration craze has spread across college football, Major League Baseball (MLB) and other sporting events, turning shirt-twirling into a viral rallying ritual.

While most people have probably only heard of this phenomenon in the last couple of months, the trend goes back much further and riffs on the slang term "tarp," referring to a shirt, that's been around even longer.

So, where did this trend originally start, and how did it become one of the defining sports fan crazes of 2026? Let's explain.

The phrase "tarps off" is slang for going shirtless, but the viral sports trend largely traces its origins to an Oklahoma State (OSU) football game back in October 2025.

During the game, fan Trent Eaton reportedly accepted a $10 bet from his sister to enter the student section, remove his shirt and wave it over his head.

A TikTok video of Eaton enthusiastically twirling his shirt while surrounded by an otherwise subdued crowd quickly went viral. As more fans joined in, the moment became the blueprint for what would later become known as the "Tarps Off" trend.

Over the following months, similar displays appeared at college football games across the United States before making the jump to professional sports and the MLB.

The movement gained renewed momentum in the spring of 2026 after fans at a Colorado Rockies game adopted the celebration, while the phrase "tarps off" itself also became increasingly common in sports clips shared online.

The trend reached a new level of popularity in May 2026 when members of the Stephen F. Austin State University baseball team attended a St. Louis Cardinals game at Busch Stadium.

Attempting to energize the crowd during a comeback, the players removed their shirts and spun them over their heads, helping spark an atmosphere that culminated in a Cardinals walk-off victory.

Videos of the celebration quickly spread across social media in May, prompting the Cardinals to embrace the movement by inviting the "Tarp Crew" to meet the team and later designating an official shirt-optional fan section in the stadium.

Throughout the summer of 2026, the tradition spread to stadiums across Major League Baseball, with fans at games involving the Tampa Bay Rays, Seattle Mariners, Detroit Tigers, Kansas City Royals, Houston Astros and other teams adopting the celebration.

The trend also inspired commentary videos, memes and parodies, including posts showing women participating, such as one shared under the "Women in Male-Dominated Fields" meme format, cementing "Tarps Off" as one of the summer's biggest sports trends.

For the full history of the Tarps Off trend, be sure to check out Know Your Meme's encyclopedia entry for even more information.

title: Jake Paul claims NFL teams have reached out to sign him to address ‘super mediocrity’ among players
description: Jake Paul might be eyeing a major career transition, as he pivots from the boxing ring to the NFL gridiron. Paul is perhaps the most polarizing figure in all of sports today.
fullText:
Jake Paul might be eyeing a major career transition, as he pivots from the boxing ring to the NFL gridiron.

Paul is perhaps the most polarizing figure in all of sports today. And he has managed to translate his notorious reputation into a lucrative career as one of the biggest draws in combat sports today.

But after a crushing defeat to Anthony Joshua in December, could Paul be leaving behind his gloves for a helmet and some shoulder pads?

Speaking to Front Office Sports, Jake Paul revealed that he has had conversations with multiple NFL teams and coaches about possibly transitioning to the NFL.

Paul then took a dig at a large number of NFL players, suggesting that he is a better athlete than them, and that he would pursue an NFL career once he wraps up his boxing career.

“It’s pretty simple. Just like when I started boxing, it’s funny to see the Tweet-and-deleters out there, the non-believers, the non-sayers, shoutout to Drake.

“I think there is a lot of super-mediocrity in the NFL, a lot of not-good athletes, a lot of people dropping passes on a consistent basis.

“I have better hands than them, I’m faster than them, I’m stronger than them, I work harder than them. Really, all it is going to take is just me after boxing, practicing some routes.

“I have a couple of teams and coaches that I have talked to that are interested in bringing me on to the team. It’s really going to be quite easy.”

When asked which team in the NFL he would want to play for, Paul claimed that he wanted to represent his hometown team, the Cleveland Browns.

“I’d love to go to the Cleveland Browns, I’ve been a Browns fan my whole entire life. My mom is a die-hard Browns fan and I think they could use some good receivers over there. Reserve the #17 Browns jersey right now, thank you.”

Paul grew up in Cleveland, so his desire to play for the Browns makes sense, especially considering their lack of success over the last two decades.

It appears Paul is trying to transition from combat sports to football, something Brock Lesnar attempted in 2004 when he left the WWE.

Lesnar managed to make it to the Minnesota Vikings practice squad before being cut, but the University of Minnesota standout had some prior high school football experience to justify the endeavor.

Paul does not have the same football experience, nor the explosive athleticism that Lesnar did, so he might find this transition a lot tougher.

title: Crystal Palace sports centre set for £130m revamp
description: Bromley Council is to meet to discuss plans for a major revamp of the world famous sport centre.
fullText:
Plans to transform and regenerate the world-leading Crystal Palace National Sports Centre are set to be approved by Bromley Council.

The scheme include a revamp of the athletics stadium, indoor arena, and swimming and diving facilities.

The project - spearheaded by the Greater London Authority (GLA) and London's mayor Sir Sadiq Khan - is to be discussed by Bromley Council on Thursday, where planning officers have recommended it for approval.

Supporters have praised the sporting opportunities the new centre will bring to south London, while objectors are concerned certain sports could be disadvantaged under the new plans.

Bromley planners said the proposal would "significantly enhance the quality of the existing sports provision and improve the experience of users across both the borough and London".

The planning application has received hundreds of responses from Bromley residents; 390 people wrote in to support the project, while the proposal also garnered 406 objections.

The battle to bring London Diamond League 'home' to Crystal Palace

Supporters have welcomed the chance to bring the dilapidated complex back to life, with one describing it as "the beating heart of Crystal Palace, much loved and used".

Others felt the centre's revival would reduce crime and anti-social behaviour in the area by increasing sporting opportunities.

Several sporting bodies have also thrown their support behind the project, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS).

England Athletics said the project would "secure the long-term future of the site and allow it to serve as a modern, inclusive, and sustainable centre for athletics".

Volleyball England "strongly supports" the regeneration, it said.

Divers have said are keen to see the diving pools brought back into use and and water polo and underwater hockey players are hopeful the 50m pool could host matches and tournaments.

Sport England said there was "overwhelming support" for the plans.

A spokesperson said: "The Crystal Palace National Sports Centre is tired and dated, and in desperate need of investment and modernisation in order to make it inclusive and accessible to all sections of the local community and to bring it into the 21st century, as well as to set in sound financial footing for the future."

However, England Hockey and the Football Foundation have objected to the plans as they think the proposed shared multi-sport artificial grass pitch would not be sufficient for the demand that both hockey and football have.

The organisations are also concerned about the loss of an artificial pitch at the centre.

The indoor climbing community has voiced several concerns about the provision for a climbing wall within the new sports centre - which is to be moved to the current 5-a-side building.

Bromley planning officers argued that the space set aside for the climbing facility was nearly three times the size of the current one.

The proposal would mean some parts of the motorsport track are built on, something objectors say "prevents its use in the future and prevents people walking the historic track".

Bromley planning officers said the entirety of the racing circuit would be retained and remain "clearly recognisable" despite the changes.

Only some sections of Stadium Straight would be narrowed to enable the inclusion of additional outdoor sporting and recreational facilities, such as 5-a-side football and 3v3 basketball.

title: LA Rams’ Matthew Stafford Falls to NFL MVP for Best QB in Latest Rankings
description: The Los Angeles Rams spent the offseason feeling like Matthew Stafford is one of the NFL’s otherworldly quarterbacks for at least one more season.A new national ranking offered an endorsement that bolstered that belief.FOX Sports’ Henry McKenna ranked all 32 projected starting quarterbacks heading into training camp and placed Stafford at No. 2.Only Buffalo Bills […] The post LA Rams’ Matthew Stafford Falls to NFL MVP for Best QB in Latest Rankings appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams spent the offseason feeling like Matthew Stafford is one of the NFL’s otherworldly quarterbacks for at least one more season.

A new national ranking offered an endorsement that bolstered that belief.

FOX Sports’ Henry McKenna ranked all 32 projected starting quarterbacks heading into training camp and placed Stafford at No. 2.

Only Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen finished above him.

Stafford landed ahead of Joe Burrow, Jordan Love, Justin Herbert, Drake Maye and Patrick Mahomes.

McKenna described the exercise as an early look toward Week 1, with quarterback readiness, supporting casts and track records among the considerations.

The placement gives the Rams another reason to enter training camp with Super Bowl expectations.

Stafford earned the ranking after producing the best statistical season of his 17-year career.

The 38-year-old led the NFL with 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdown passes while throwing eight interceptions. He also finished second with a 109.2 passer rating, led the league with 236 passing first downs and helped Los Angeles finish 12-5.

His efficiency became historic during the middle of the season.

Stafford became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw at least four touchdown passes without an interception in three consecutive regular-season games. He later set a league record by throwing 28 consecutive touchdown passes without an interception.

Those numbers earned Stafford the first Associated Press NFL MVP of his career and a first Associated Press NFL MVP. The Rams then signed him to a contract extension in May, removing one potential distraction before his 18th season.

The ranking still stopped one place short of putting Stafford at the top.

Allen passed for 3,668 yards with 25 touchdowns and 10 interceptions last season, although his rushing ability continues to give Buffalo another dimension.

FOX Sports nevertheless placed Stafford above several younger quarterbacks carrying their own championship expectations.

That group includes Mahomes, who fell to No. 7 as he works back from a torn ACL, and Burrow, who ranked third after an injury-shortened season.

For Stafford, No. 2 represents another sign that age has done little to weaken his standing around the league.

The regular-season production only tells part of the story.

Stafford completed 22 of 35 passes for 374 yards and three touchdowns in the NFC Championship Game. The Rams still fell 31-27 to the Seattle Seahawks after defensive and special teams mistakes left the offense chasing the game.

According to the Rams, Stafford became the first quarterback to throw for at least 350 yards and three touchdowns without a turnover and lose a playoff start. Puka Nacua caught nine passes for 165 yards and a touchdown, but Los Angeles could not complete its final comeback.

That ending reinforced how close the Rams are to another Super Bowl appearance.

Los Angeles selected Ty Simpson with the No. 13 pick in the 2026 NFL draft as Stafford’s eventual successor. The Rams have not established a timeline for that transition, and Stafford said during organized team activities that his body felt good as he prepared for another season.

Training camp begins July 27 at Loyola Marymount University. The Rams can manage Stafford’s workload while developing the depth behind him, but there is little uncertainty about which quarterback determines the team’s ceiling.

FOX Sports placed Stafford behind one quarterback in the league.

After an MVP season and a narrow NFC Championship Game loss, the Rams enter camp with expectations to match that ranking.

Stafford has already shown he can play at the required level. The next challenge is turning it into one more Super Bowl run.

title: Five big names to look out for at Commonwealth Games
description: These are the stars to look out for across the 10 sports at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
fullText:
With 215 golds up for grabs at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, highlighting just five medal hopefuls is no easy feat.

title: SEC commish throws cold water on 'breakaway' notion, but concerns abound with Senate bill still up for grabs
description: 'If the headline remains that we’re breaking away, that’s uninformed,' Greg Sankey told Yahoo Sports.
fullText:
TAMPA, Fla. – Within this waterfront Marriott hotel along an offshoot of Tampa Bay, college football’s biggest media extravaganza unfolds.

In the main grand hallway, where hundreds of press members gather here for SEC football media days, a giant logo portraying the conference’s three iconic letters — S-E-C — serves as the primary visual backdrop.

But adjacent to that display, behind a guarded curtain, the league’s commissioner slumps into a chair as he scrolls through his cell phone during a rare quiet moment amidst the bustle.

“Mmm,” he mutters as he glares at the screen. “More messages from Washington.”

A topic at this year’s event — even among the head football coaches themselves — is ongoing negotiations over a congressional bill to regulate college athletics and, perhaps even more notable, the SEC’s potential plans, without revised federal legislation, to operate within its own silo: a conference-led governance model that’s caused a stir across the country.

In fact, in a sitdown with Yahoo Sports, Greg Sankey says the frustration within his league over the absence of regulation and enforcement will “continue to simmer” and “if we’re not able to deal with issues, then the boil starts.”

Does that mean the SEC intends to execute a full-fledged breakaway from the NCAA umbrella, to remove itself from the College Football Playoff and NCAA championships, to only play itself in the regular season, hold its own postseason tournament and then, if another league’s champion wants to duel, play them in a neutral-site game deemed as the new national championship?

But it does mean that the SEC is exploring a self-governing model to create and then enforce its own rules related to eligibility, transfers and athlete compensation.

However, he’s made clear in a recommendation to university presidents that it is not his preferred course of action. What is? A congressional bill.

While coaches parade across media day here, lawmakers and staff members in Washington, D.C. are continuing intense negotiations over revisions to the Protect College Sports Act in an effort to gain the support of the SEC and Big Ten. In fact, Big Ten commissioner Tony Petitti, on the Hill this week, has been an active, in-person participant in the negotiations with the bill’s co-authors Sens. Ted Cruz, Maria Cantwell and Eric Schmitt. ACC commissioner Jim Phillips was scheduled to be on the Hill on Wednesday too.

Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark and Sankey, from the enclave at media days, have participated by phone.

Without a bill, the SEC’s conference-led governance model “takes on more interest,” said Sankey. “But that doesn’t mean something is poised to happen.”

“If the headline remains that we’re breaking away, that’s uninformed,” he told Yahoo Sports.

Those with knowledge of negotiations over the Senate bill have expressed renewed confidence in reaching an agreement with the two conferences over supporting the legislation — a key to the bill moving through the Senate, then the House and being signed by the president.

The latest discussions have centered mostly on changes to the revenue-share cap. Lawmakers are discussing the creation of a separate retention pool of money — $25 million in addition to the $21.3 million cap — that schools can use for the sole purpose of retaining athletes currently on their roster.

Cap adjustments are necessary, Sankey told Yahoo Sports, but he’d prefer to see finalized texts before commenting on the retention pool.

A litany of other issues languish as lawmakers and staff members work to reach a compromise on revisions, both between themselves — the Republican Cruz and Democrat Cantwell — and with leaders of the SEC and Big Ten.

For instance, an anti-expansion provision remains a fluid subject that, as of the latest discussions, would cap conference membership at 19 schools and require programs moving from one power conference to another to operate as an independent for five years. Such a move may expedite another wave of conference expansion as schools jockey to elevate themselves — such as ACC programs moving to the Big Ten or SEC — before the bill passes.

Lawmakers are expected to add to the legislation a provision that prohibits third-party entities, such as private equity firms, from creating a super league by poaching the top 20-30 brands in the country in a move to generate millions 

Asked why he’s so concerned about such entities forming a super league, Sankey told Yahoo Sports, “Because that’s what their proposals contemplate. You can define it however you want to, but my view is, whether it’s 20, 30, 70, 130 [schools], you are really creating a super league. There’s no assurance that once that project is down the road and it can't generate the income it’s promised for 130, that they don’t scale back to something very different.”

Sankey often refers to the SEC as its own “super league.” And many within his conference believe that the SEC should not only govern itself but only compete against itself — a model spearheaded publicly by Georgia president Jere Morehead.

“l think we’d want to play with the schools following the rules,” Morehead told Yahoo Sports earlier this year.

A conference-only governance model is rife with its own problems, let alone the revolutionary action of competitively leaving everyone behind. Sankey holds a background in college compliance and said a league enforcing its own rules would be “very” difficult. It’s why many conferences, including the SEC, abandoned such a structure years ago and instead granted the NCAA control over regulation and enforcement.

When he joined the SEC, Sankey told then-commissioner Mike Slive that he did not want the role of “head of enforcement” because of the difficulties associated with the league penalizing its own member schools.

And what about a competitive breakaway? Starting your own playoff? Playing only yourself?

The ideas have been discussed among administrators as a “Plan B” if federal legislation doesn’t pass. But, Sankey said, the plan may lead to political problems with the same entity, Congress, that officials are lobbying for assistance.

“It doesn’t take much imagination to say we’re going to leave [competitively] and you’re in congressional hearings [answering for it]. I think that’s unwise.”

title: NBC earns best Open Championship audience since 2022
