fullText:
American sports fans looking for an appetizer prior to Sunday’s World Cup final seemed to get one in the 154th Open Championship.

NBC’s final-round coverage of the last men’s golf major of the year averaged 4.3 million viewers, up six percent from last year’s victory from Scottie Scheffler at Royal Portrush (4.1 million viewers). Ryan Fox’s dramatic win capped with a birdie on the 72nd hole peaked at 6.1 million viewers during the 1:15 p.m. ET quarter-hour.

As usual, the Open Championship was the least-watched of the four majors due to a less favorable time zone for the American audience. NBC’s final-round window began at 9 a.m. and went through 2 p.m. ET, whereas final-round coverage of the Masters, for instance, begins at 2 p.m. and typically runs until about 7 p.m. ET. Those Sunday afternoon hours are prime viewing times for the U.S. audience. Sunday morning? Not so much.

As Sports Business Journal’s Josh Carpenter lays out, June’s U.S. Open averaged 5.5 million viewers in the final round, the PGA Championship 5.7 million viewers in May, and the Masters 13.9 million viewers in April.

NBC: 4.3 million viewers for the final round of @TheOpen, its best since 2022, though with the addition of Big Data, fair to wonder if last year (4.1M) would have outdrawn it.

Major viewership this year (final rounds)

Masters: 13.9M
 PGA: 5.7M
 U.S. Open: 5.5M
 Open: 4.3M pic.twitter.com/1jvOdTBxTz

— Josh Carpenter (@JoshACarpenter) July 21, 2026

Still, holding an audience of 4.3 million viewers across a five-hour window early on Sunday is a solid result for NBC. It should be noted, this is the first Open Championship to be measured using Nielsen’s new Big Data + Panel standard, and the six percent year-over-year increase falls within the range that could solely be explained by the changes.

Saturday saw a larger year-over-year bump, however. Third-round coverage on NBC and Peacock averaged 3.7 million viewers, up 16 percent versus last year (3.2 million viewers) and good for the most-watched third round since 2018.

title: 'Would Beckham do it?' - Fury stands by Thailand fight

fullText:
Boxer Tyson Fury says modern-day sports stars think they are "bigger than they actually are" after choosing to fight in front of just 1,500 fans in Thailand instead of pursuing a more lucrative event elsewhere.

The former heavyweight world champion, 37, will face 46-year-old Pole Mariusz Wach in Pattaya on Friday.

"Which other world champion on my level - a high-level athlete on earth - would do a performance in front of 1,500 in Pattaya?" Fury said at Wednesday's news conference.

"Do you think David Beckham would play professional football here, or someone famous like that? No way. They're just not going to do it.

"A lot of these big celebrities and sports stars think they're bigger than they actually are."

Adversity to history - Agyarko's world title dream

Friday's contest will not be broadcast live and will instead feature as part of the third series of the Netflix documentary 'At Home with the Furys'.

The proposed Fury-Joshua fight has been more than a decade in the making, with contracts already signed for a contest expected later this year, although a venue has yet to be confirmed.

Wach has lost seven of his past 10 fights and is a significant underdog on paper, but Fury insisted the veteran presents a sterner test than Joshua's opponent, Albanian Prenga.

"Let me tell you, Mariusz Wach would put his fist through Joshua's opponent, whoever he is," Fury said.

"This man would knock him spark out. He's a real fighting man. We're not interested in other people. This is my show.

"I'm not interested in what's going on elsewhere with Joshua or [Deontay] Wilder or [Oleksandr] Usyk or anybody. This is about me and Mariusz, not about anybody else.

"What happens beyond Friday is none of my concern. What will be will be."

The event was organised on just three weeks' notice after Fury decided he wanted to fight in Thailand, with promoter Spencer Brown saying the former champion turned down the opportunity to earn considerably more elsewhere.

Brown also says ticket profits will be donated to a local charity supporting disadvantaged children and students with disabilities.

Fury, who bases his training camps in Thailand, appeared relaxed and in good spirits. Wearing shorts and a T-shirt, he said he felt revitalised by returning to the country.

"I feel at peace with everything whereas before I had a lot of pressure on me," he said.

"I thrive better in a warmer climate and feel rejuvenated."

Fury criticised the current heavyweight champions - WBC title-holder Agit Kabayel, WBA champion Murat Gassiev and WBO champion Daniel Dubois.

Kabayel and Gassiev became world champions after Usyk vacated his belts, while Dubois claimed the title by beating Fabio Wardley in May.

"All those men have been gifted world titles and never actually fought anyone to get them," he said.

"How can you compare those men to me? I've fought legends in the game and beat them for the titles. They're in their own little group and I'm on top of the Empire State Building."

Wach promised to "ruin" any plans for a Fury-Joshua fight by causing an upset in Pattaya.

Fury quickly dismissed the suggestion he was overlooking his opponent.

"No," he replied. "I'm focused on you only. Zero interest in Joshua."

title: Jeff Bezos ‘approached’ to join consortium in talks over Liverpool investment
description: Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group have confirmed that a consortium led by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia is in talks over a minority investment
fullText:
Jeff Bezos, the Amazon founder and fourth-richest man in the world, has been “approached” by a consortium that is in talks to buy a minority stake in Liverpool, according to reports.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group confirmed on Tuesday that they had been approached by a consortium led by Amit Bhatia, the British-Indian millionaire and former co-owner of QPR.

Sky News reported that Bezos has held “discussions” with the group, with talks still at an early stage.

Bezos, whose fortune is reportedly worth $257bn and who owns the Washington Post, explored bids for two NFL teams last year, the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders, but did not proceed with either deal.

A spokesperson for FSG said on Tuesday: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.”

Bhatia, the son-in-law of Lakshimi Mittal, the billionaire executive of steel production giant ArcelorMittal, also confirmed his departure from QPR’s board on Tuesday, the same day as FSG confirmed the talks with his consortium.

FSG sold a minority stake in Liverpool to investment firm Dynasty in 2023, which brought an injection of cash into the club following the pandemic, but did not fund future transfers.

title: Liverpool owner FSG in talks to sell minority stake to former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia
description: Fenway Sports Group acknowledged the approach on the same day that Bhatia stepped down from the board at QPR after 18 years at the club
fullText:
A consortium led by British-Indian millionaire Amit Bhatia, formerly a co-owner of QPR, has expressed interest in acquiring a minority stake in Liverpool Football Club.

Owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed they had been approached regarding the potential investment.

This development coincides with Bhatia's departure from the QPR board, concluding an 18-year involvement, after agreeing to transfer his shares to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

A spokesperson for FSG said: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.”

No deal has been agreed with discussions at an early stage.

In 2023, FSG sold a minority stake in Liverpool to investment firm Dynasty and any deal with Bhatia, should it proceed, is expected to be along similar lines.

FSG, which also owns the Boston Red Sox and the Pittsburgh Penguins, bought Liverpool in 2010 for £300million. Forbes recently valued the club at £4.6billion.

On Tuesday, Bhatia announced he was leaving his role at QPR. He served as vice-chairman before becoming chairman in 2018, a role he held for five years.

In quotes on the QPR website, the 46-year-old said: “Since joining the club in 2007, QPR has been a deeply important part of my life and of my family’s life.

“Over nearly two decades we have shared promotions, relegations, unforgettable highs and painful lows, and the memories we have made at Loftus Road alongside the supporters will stay with us forever.

“I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection. I want to thank the players, managers, staff, the community trust, my fellow board members and, above all, the fans, who have made me and my family feel part of the QPR family for so many years.”

“QPR will always have a very special place in my heart,” he added.

Bhatia is the son-in-law of Lakshimi Mittal, executive of steel and mining company ArcelorMittal. Forbes has recently valued Mittal’s fortune at £23.2billion.

In May of this year, Mittal partnered with Adal Poonawalla to buy a controlling stake in the Indian Premier League team Rajasthan Royals.

fullText:
Another round of layoffs has arrived in Bristol, Connecticut as ESPN prepares to say goodbye to many household names. But none may be bigger than longtime veteran anchor and play-by-play man Karl Ravech.

Both The Athletic and Front Office Sports broke the news of Ravech’s ESPN departure on Tuesday morning. ESPN is preparing to do what is now seemingly their annual custom of summer layoffs to balance their books, painfully saying goodbye to several on-air personalities in addition to folks behind the scenes.

The most recent wave of layoffs got underway on Monday night with the shock departure of longtime NFL analyst Ryan Clark. As the news broke of Clark’s termination, he was live on the network airwaves on NFL Live and was informed during the program of his fate in a sad and stunning turn of events. While he was the first name to be shared, others are expected to follow, especially centered on the newly acquired NFL Network.

However, Ravech is reportedly the biggest name to be let go as part of these 2026 layoffs given his decades of contributions to ESPN.

Karl Ravech was a mainstay at ESPN as a SportsCenter anchor and the longtime host of Baseball Tonight, which at one time was a nightly staple on the WorldWide Leader in Sports. He was also the host of ESPN’s on-site World Series coverage. In recent years, he transitioned to being one of ESPN’s lead play-by-play announcers for the sport, calling the famed Sunday Night Baseball franchise before it moved on to NBC this season.

Ravech first joined ESPN in May 1993. Although he was synonymous with the network’s baseball coverage for much of that time period, he was also a longtime SportsCenter anchor and called college basketball games for the network.

The news of Ravech’s departure came just one night after he called the Los Angeles Dodgers vs Philadelphia Phillies contest on ESPN in what may end up being his last assignment for the network. It remains to be seen where ESPN goes for the remainder of their baseball coverage in 2026. But seeing Karl Ravech exit the network mid-season in this way after so many dedicated years of service in Bristol is a sobering reminder of the current realities of modern media.

title: Soccer legend moving on from broadcasting following World Cup: ‘Farewell to the studio’
description: Former Swedish soccer star Zlatan Ibrahimovic is moving on from broadcasting after making his debut with FOX Sports for the World Cup.
fullText:
Swedish soccer legend Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who joined FOX Sports as an analyst for the World Cup, is moving on from broadcasting.

Ibrahimovic announced following Sunday’s final between Spain and Argentina that the 2026 World Cup will be his one and only event as a broadcaster.

“I’ve been talking a lot the last one and a half months, so these will be my last words,” Ibrahimovic said on air. “It has been an absolutely pleasure to share this studio with you guys. You made it very easy for me. I want to thank also FOX studio, I want to thank America, I want to thank also all the other people you don’t see. … You made it easy for me.

“I hope America, you enjoyed it as much as I did. And this is also my farewell to the studio. This was the first and last time for me, so thank you everybody.”

Ibrahimovic drew widespread praise throughout the World Cup for his work as an analyst.

Andrew Marchand, who covers sports media for The Athletic, described him as “a World Cup TV star.”

Still, Sweden’s all-time leading goal scorer says he is moving on from broadcasting.

In addition to playing for the Swedish national team, Ibrahimovic also played for AC Milan, FC Barcelona, Inter Milan, Juventus, Manchester United, Paris Saint-Germain and other professional teams during his career.

He scored 62 goals with the Swedish national team and is considered to be one of the best goal scorers in soccer history.

fullText:
After Yahoo! Sports reported last week the SEC was considering “Plan B” amid talks about the Protect College Sports Act, commissioner Greg Sankey confirmed those talks are not just a negotiating play. He said the discussions are “real” as the college athletics landscape shifts.

“You phrased the question, ‘How real?’ So I’ll take that as, like, real or not. So they’re real,” Sankey said at SEC media days. “People have talked about that. They’ve opined about the frustrations that bring them to the point of saying we should look at something significantly different.

“I do not believe that is a leverage point. I think that’s just honest communication. I would prefer that stay in a meeting room or on a video conference and not be part of the D1.ticker the next morning, but I don’t control all of that.”

title: Vote for the best Vermont high school sports dynasty of the last 50 years powered by Delta Dental
description: It's time to vote for Vermont's best high school sports dynasty of the last 50 years powered by Delta Dental.
fullText:
From yearslong championship runs and sheer dominance to impressive consecutive winning streaks, dynastic programs are weaved into high school sports history in Vermont. And over the last 50 years, this state has seen its share of tradition-rich programs rack up wins and titles, from a diverse offering of sports.

But which dynasty is the greatest? To answer that question, Burlington Free Press reporters Alex Abrami and Judith Altneu plucked out 20 deserving nominations of the last five decades. Now it's your turn, the reader, to cast your vote in the latest BFP summer ballot powered by Delta Dental.

For a starting point in this subjective process, the Free Press looked at teams with at least five years (or more) of extended greatness.

Read on and then vote away! Print readers can find the poll at burlingtonfreepress.com.

After back-to-back penalty shootout losses, the former in one of the state's great upsets, the Champlain Valley boys soccer program reeled off six consecutive Division I state titles (counting a tie in 2003 with BFA-St. Albans). Led by Dan Shepardson for the first four and his former player T.J. Mead for the last two, the Redhawks went 94-5-5 over their championship run.

Since 2011, the CVU girls soccer team has captured 11 D-I crowns and finished runner-up twice with seven unbeaten seasons. Stan Williams, who stepped down after the 2024 season, has helmed the majority of the run, with eight titles and a 182-9-6 record over a dozen years that includes a 61-game winning streak from 2017-2020.

Since 2003, the CVU girls cross-country running team has raced to 21 out of 23 D-I titles, including 12 in a row from 2009-2020 under former coach Scott Bliss. But Redhawks are also a regional powerhouse, with nine New England crowns (2003, 2010, 2011, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2023, 2024, 2025) and five appearances at nationals (2010, 2011, 2018, 2024, 2025).

Since volleyball became a varsity sport in 2016, Essex girls volleyball has appeared in every championship game winning seven of the nine possible titles. Jen Liguori leads a team that has posted five straight undefeated seasons with an 86-game winning streak dating back to 2021.

Hartford field hockey dominated Division II winning four consecutive titles from 1994-1997 (one tie) with current head coach Heather Scudder at the helm. The Hurricanes moved up to Division I in 1998 and proceeded to advance to seven straight championship games from 1999-2005, winning six straight titles (includes one tie in in 2002).

Between 2007-2012, Hartford football stormed to five D-I titles, including three straight from 2010-12. The Hurricanes are the lone D-I team to seize a three-peat and they owned a 27-game winning streak that stretched over four seasons. In two of their perfect seasons, the Hurricanes tallied 915 points over 22 games while rushing for 4,056 yards in 2012.

Under coach Mike Gonneville, Northfield girls soccer ripped off a 69-game winning streak, the nation's third longest at the time, and seven straight titles in D-III between 1995-2001. The Marauders also had a 74-game unbeaten streak snapped in 2000. Over the seven championship seasons, Northfield went 114-8-2. After losing in the semis in 2002, Northfield then proceeded to three-peat.

Stowe boys soccer seized seven straight D-III championships between 2012-2018. Then the Raiders jumped to D-II and captured the 2019 title for eight in a row and an unbeaten season at 17-0-1. Brian Buczek led Stowe to six of those crowns and went 86-11-8 in his tenure.

In the early days of hockey, it's no surprise BFA-St. Albans was the team to beat. The Bobwhites claimed seven D-I championships in a row between 1973-79, with a pair of unbeaten seasons that includes 18-0 in 1975 when they blasted Spaulding 7-3 in the final. During the seven-year run, BFA went 114-11-2.

BFA-St. Albans has been the state's most consistent girls hockey program since the Vermont Principals' Association added the sport staring with the the 2001-2002 season. The Comets lead the state with 13 girls hockey championships and won the first five D-I titles (2002-2006). Longtime head coach Luke Cioffi has guided BFA to appearances in 19 of the state's 25 championship games.

When CVU girls basketball won in 2013, the Redhawks ended a 26-year title drought. More titles and more wins kept flowing: Under coach Ute Otley's direction, CVU seized five straight D-I crowns and compiled a 96-game winning streak that set a Vermont all-time modern record. In four out of the five seasons, a Redhawk was named the Free Press' Miss Basketball including Emily Kinneston in back-to-back years (2013, 2014).

Essex girls basketball dominated the sport in the late 1990s, posting back-to-back undefeated seasons in 1995 and 1996 and accumulated a 63-game winning streak. Libby Smith was the star for the Hornets during their five-year consecutive championship run. The Hornets would add their third undefeated season in four seasons in 1998 before losing in the 1999 and 2000 championship games.

Essex dominated gymnastics, winning every championship meet over a dozen years between 2006-2017. The Hornets also had every all-around state champion over their run, paced by Mary Savage (Krug), who seized four straight wins from 2006-09.

Mount Anthony boys basketball had one of Vermont's most dominant runs in the sport capturing five straight Division I championships. During that five-year run, head coach Dave Fredrickson compiled a 102-13 record. To earn that last title in 1992, Mount Anthony rallied late in the fourth quarter and pulled away in overtime for a 56-51 win over Colchester.

Mount Anthony wrestling had its remarkable championship run earlier this year. But the Patriots have truly been kings of their sport in Vermont. They seized 36 straight state titles, a national record for wrestling programs and the sixth most out of all sports according to NFHS. The Patriots, led by national coach of the year honoree Scott Legacy for the majority of their reign, also feasted on their competition out of state, racking up eight New England crowns and seven runner-up finishes since 1989.

During Essex's girls track and field's historic run, three different coaches — Steve Dowd, Karen Albright and Joe Gonillo — led the program, but the standard remained consistent. In Gonillo's first season as the girls coach in 1997, Essex set a then-national record for the sport, capturing its 13th straight Division I title. During that 13-year stretch the Hornets claimed 38 individual titles and set five state records.

Champlain Valley boys lacrosse have been a tough out come postseason time no matter its seed. The Redhawks have won 12 of the last 13 Division I lacrosse titles, including a record-setting nine in a row. The only year CVU did not win came in 2023 when they got bounced in the semifinals. Three of the Redhawks titles came when they were seeded fourth or lower including their 2025 title.

For six seasons in the mid-2000s, Lyndon softball dominated the sport winning 79-straight games from 2005-2009 and four straight D-II titles. Three of those state championships were decided in one-run games. Sandwiched between that four-peat, Lyndon suffered losses in the 2004 and 2009 D-II title games.

The South Burlington boys tennis team went on a tear in the late 1980s-1990s with record-setting coach Steve LaTulippe who won over 200 matches during his tenure. South Burlington captured seven consecutive titles with five total undefeated seasons during its dynasty. South Burlington lead the state with 25 total boys tennis championships.

After finishing as the runner-ups in 1995, South Burlington girls tennis used that loss as motivation fueling an extended run where the team advanced to 12 straight championship matches, winning nine total titles under longtime coach Jake Agna, who retired prior to the 2023 season. That run also covers a five-peat from 1999-2003, during which Sara Hughes claimed four straight individual titles.

title: LA sports figure Jeff Pearlman admits Angels have helped him ‘rediscover his love for baseball’
description: It’s been a long and exhausting season for the Angels, but it appears the team has helped at least one fan rediscover his love for baseball. New York Times award-winning...
fullText:
It’s been a long and exhausting season for the Angels, but it appears the team has helped at least one fan rediscover his love for baseball.

New York Times award-winning sports author Jeff Pearlman released a video on TikTok, revealing the Angels have rekindled his passion for the sport.

“In the last [month] I’ve gone to probably like five games, three of the five just by myself, and you may think, ‘What kind of loser goes to a baseball game by himself?’ It’s [the] best,” Pearlman said during the TikTok video. “I buy a ticket really high up. … I get free parking because I park offsite, and I just love it.”

“I love the feel of the ballpark, I love the look of the ballpark, I love the green, I love the national anthem, the seventh-inning stretch, I love that the Angels always do these really cheesy giveaways.”

Despite the Angels having a poor record (39-61), Pearlman said he enjoys being able to watch baseball at an affordable price and called it the “cheapest, best bang for your buck ever.”

Pearlman went on to compare how cheap the Angels tickets are compared with Dodgers tickets. He said he’s happy not having to spend $40 to park and spending over $100 for a ticket.

Pearlman is a New York Times best-selling author who writes about football, baseball and basketball. He also wrote a biography on Tupac Shakur.

Some notable books Pearlman has written about LA sports in his career include “Showtime: Magic, Kareem, Riley, and the Los Angeles Lakers Dynasty of the 1980s,” and “Three-Ring Circus: Kobe, Shaq, Phil, and the Crazy Years of the Lakers Dynasty.”

Now attending Angels games for the experience to watch baseball in its purest form, Pearlman said he’s been taking photos with fans in attendance and leaving free copies of his books across the stadium. He enjoys getting a cold brew coffee from the Rise Espresso Bar in the stadium that includes cold foam and Cocoa Puffs.

The 2026 season has been another tough one for Angels fans, and the franchise might lose 100 games in a season for the first time.

Fans at Angel Stadium have been voicing their frustrations toward ownership this year. Earlier this season, they organized protests toward owner Arte Moreno, urging him to sell the team due to another losing season.

The protests have also been happening inside the stadium as fans have been participating in the Tarps Off movement, which has included regular chants of “Sell the team,” echoing from the right field seats.

Pearlman admitted he has mixed feelings about Tarps Off but called it “entertaining.”

“My new happy place is going to Angels games, parking for free, knowing I have a $5 ticket, watching the game, presuming the Angels are probably going to lose,” Pearlman said. “Just relishing in the moment.”

title: Where did MSU's Pat Fitzgerald land in CBS Sports' annual hot seat rankings?
description: See where Michigan State's Pat Fitzgerald landed in CBS Sports' hot seat rankings for the upcoming season
fullText:
Michigan State head coach Pat Fitzgerald is considered one of the safest coaches in all of college football as we near the 2026 season.

CBS Sports has released their annual hot seat ratings and rankings for all of the FBS head coaches, and to no surprise, the newly hired Fitzgerald is sitting on a very cool seat at the moment. On a rating system of zero through five, Fitzgerald landed with a 0.7 rating -- which is considered "untouchable" at the moment.

Fitzgerald is set to enter his first season as the Spartans head coach after taking over for Jonathan Smith, who was fired after only two years at Michigan State. The man who hired Fitzgerald, though, is no longer around as former athletic director J Batt is now off to Kentucky after only one year of running the Spartans' athletics department. So it's interesting to see Fitzgerald have such a low hot seat rating among his peers.

For some perspective, new Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham has a rating of 1.5 -- which is notably higher than Fitzgerald. One would assume that would be higher due to the Wolverines having higher expectations to win big this year compared to the Spartans.

title: Zlatan Ibrahimovic announces Fox decision after World Cup
description: Excitement arose among soccer fans around the world when it was announced that Zlatan Ibrahimovic will serve as an analyst for the FIFA World Cup. He worked alongside Alexi Lalas and Thierry Henry for Fox Sports’ coverage and gave entertaining…
fullText:
Excitement arose among soccer fans around the world when it was announced that Zlatan Ibrahimovic will serve as an analyst for the FIFA World Cup. He worked alongside Alexi Lalas and Thierry Henry for Fox Sports’ coverage and gave entertaining insights about games and players.

However, the legend announced after Sunday’s final that he will not return. He bid the network goodbye and stressed that he will not cover future World Cups.

“”And this is also my farewell to the studio,” Ibrahimovic said. “This was the first and last time for me. So, take care, everybody.”

Ibrahimovic anchored the Los Angeles-based studio team, contributing to pregame, halftime and postgame shows. He gave highly entertaining analysis in true Zlatan fashion, endearing him more to fans who supported him throughout his playing career.

The 44-year-old hung his cleats up for good in 2022 following AC Milan’s final game of the season. He started his senior club career with Malmo FF before playing for Ajax, Juventus and Inter Milan. Ibrahimovic then moved to Barcelona, AC Milan, Paris Saint-German and Manchester United. He also suited up for the LA Galaxy before returning to Italy to end his career there.

Ibrahimovic won league titles in the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, France and England. He also suited up for Sweden in international competitions, establishing himself as one of the best forwards in the world. His flamboyant playing style and larger-than-life persona made him an influential figure in the sport.
